title: Separate pull-request validation from repository mutation workflows

phases.objective: Keep pull-request-triggered E2E, fanout, and supervisor validation read-only while retaining only explicitly dispatched, SHA-bound fanout mutation.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A pull request changes one of the three governed workflow surfaces.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Pull-request jobs have no write authority, the obsolete Work Map bridge is removed, fanout apply is explicitly dispatched and exact-head guarded, and supervisor assurance publishes evidence without issue mutation.
steps: Remove the pull-request-triggered Work Map mutation bridge and its connectivity registration.
Split fanout reporting from the explicitly dispatched apply workflow.
Require exact target-branch head identity and reject main and Production before fanout mutation.
Remove issue mutation from the pull-request-capable supervisor assurance workflow.
Run connectivity, fanout, supervisor, lifecycle, and changed-range E2E integrity checks.
assertions: E2E reference integrity remains pull-request-triggered and read-only.
Fanout pull-request reporting has contents read only and no push path.
Fanout apply has workflow_dispatch, expected_head_sha verification, protected-branch rejection, and no force push.
Supervisor assurance has contents read only and no issue mutation.
No Production, provider, credential, SQL, Migration Apply, database, deployment, protected-ref, Work Map publication, or external mutation is authorized.

phases.objective: Confirm exact-head pull-request jobs execute read-only and the manual fanout writer remains dormant without explicit dispatch.
Reject any reintroduction of pull-request write permissions, stale expected-head mutation, protected-branch targeting, or force push.
Observe one read-only pull-request cycle and one report-only manual cycle without invoking fanout apply.
Retain repository validation availability without granting Production or external runtime authority.
